# Rome 46 BC – Medicine & hygiene

- **Contagion by invisible living agents (germ theory)** [`contagion_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/contagion_theory.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Fevers come from marsh air, epidemics from gods. Lucretius writes of seeds of disease in the air; Varro will write (37 BC) of invisible marsh creatures. Nobody acts on it. Local: Marcus Terentius Varro; Lucretius, De rerum natura, book 6.
- **Abandoning bloodletting, purging and mercury (end of humoral medicine)** [`bloodletting_harm`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bloodletting_harm.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Greek physicians bleed, purge and give emetics. The fashionable school of Asclepiades prefers diet, wine, baths and massage, but still bleeds. Old Roman households trust cabbage and charms. Local: followers of Asclepiades of Bithynia in Rome; Cato, De agri cultura 156-157 (cabbage as a cure-all).
- **Counting and mapping cases to find causes (epidemiology)** [`epidemiology_mapping`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/epidemiology_mapping.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. The state counts citizens, not deaths or causes. Caesar's clerks have just recounted grain recipients street by street through tenement landlords; the same method would work for the sick. Local: Caesar's recount of grain recipients by district (46 BC); undertakers at the grove of Libitina on the Esquiline.
- **Hand washing with soap** [`hand_hygiene`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hand_hygiene.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. People clean themselves with oil and a strigil at the baths and rinse hands at table. No soap. Physicians and midwives see no link between hands and fever.
- **Boiling drinking water and protecting wells** [`boiled_water`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/boiled_water.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The Hippocratic Airs, Waters, Places advises boiling some waters. Romans judge water by taste and clarity and drink it mixed with wine. Fuel is dear for tenement dwellers. Local: Aqua Marcia (the best water); Tiber water and wells in the low quarters.
- **Slow sand filtration and chlorination of town water** [`water_filtration_chlorination`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/water_filtration_chlorination.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Four aqueducts: Appia, Anio Vetus, Marcia, Tepula. The Anio Vetus takes river water and runs muddy after rain. Masons could build sand filter beds; chlorination is out of reach. Local: Aqua Appia, Anio Vetus, Aqua Marcia, Aqua Tepula; aediles and censors, who oversee the water.
- **Latrines and sewers (keeping excrement out of water, food and soil)** [`sanitation_sewerage`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sanitation_sewerage.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. The Cloaca Maxima and street drains were built to drain land and carry off rain; they empty into the Tiber. Tenements use cesspits and chamber pots. Fullers collect urine. Local: Cloaca Maxima; aediles (street cleaning); fullers' urine jars at street corners.
- **Food hygiene (cooking, flies, carriers)** [`food_hygiene`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/food_hygiene.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Aediles police the markets and bad smell is the test of food. Cookshops feed the tenement population. Flies, cooks' hands and carriers are no one's concern. Local: Macellum (food market north of the Forum); aediles; popinae (cookshops).
- **Quarantine and isolation of the sick** [`quarantine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/quarantine.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. An epidemic is a prodigy, answered by consulting the Sibylline books, processions and banquets for the gods. Thucydides' remark that carers caught the Athenian plague is known to readers. Local: quindecimviri sacris faciundis (keepers of the Sibylline books); temple of Aesculapius on the Tiber Island.
- **Hospital hygiene and trained nursing** [`nursing_hospital_hygiene`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/nursing_hospital_hygiene.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. No hospitals. The sick lie at home, tended by family or slaves; the poor sleep in the temple of Aesculapius hoping for a dream. Legions have no fixed infirmaries yet. Local: temple of Aesculapius on the Tiber Island (founded 291 BC). Elsewhere: India, Ashoka's 3rd-century BC edicts on medical care (rumour at best).
- **Cholera and typhoid spread through drinking water** [`cholera_waterborne`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cholera_waterborne.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Asiatic cholera is confined to India. Greek 'cholera' means any violent vomiting and flux. Typhoid and dysentery are common, worst in army camps and late summer.
- **Oral rehydration (water, salt and sugar)** [`oral_rehydration`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oral_rehydration.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. No sugar, but honey and salt in boiled water serve. Physicians give barley water or honey water, and some deliberately withhold drink in fever.
- **Plague carried by rats and fleas (and by coughing)** [`plague_vectors`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/plague_vectors.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Bubonic plague is not in Italy; 'pestilentia' means any epidemic. Rats infest the granaries and ships. The knowledge has no visible use here for six centuries.
- **Typhus carried by body lice (delousing)** [`typhus_lice`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/typhus_lice.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Lice are ordinary, in camps and tenements alike. No epidemic of this period can be identified as typhus. Baking or boiling clothes is cheap; the reason would be new.
- **Malaria carried by mosquitoes (drainage, nets)** [`malaria_mosquito`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/malaria_mosquito.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Tertian and quartan fevers return each late summer; Fever has a shrine. Blamed on marsh air, so villas sit on hills. Caesar will plan draining the Pomptine marshes (44 BC). Local: Marcus Terentius Varro; shrine of Febris on the Palatine; Pomptine marshes and the Campagna; conopeum (Egyptian-style gnat net). Elsewhere: Egypt, marsh dwellers sleeping under nets (Herodotus).
- **Cinchona bark (quinine) against malaria** [`quinine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/quinine.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept high. Cinchona grows only in the Andes. Quartan fever is met with diet, emetics, amulets and vows to Febris. Elsewhere: Andean forests, source of cinchona bark.
- **Consumption (tuberculosis) is contagious** [`tuberculosis_control`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/tuberculosis_control.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Phthisis is well described since Hippocrates and blamed on constitution and family. The Aristotelian Problems ask why it passes to those nearby. Sea voyages and milk are prescribed.
- **Parasitic worms (hookworm, roundworm, tapeworm, guinea worm)** [`parasitic_worms`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/parasitic_worms.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Flat and round worms are distinguished and thought to breed from gut decay. Pomegranate (Cato 126-127) and male fern are real remedies. Transmission by soil, pork and water is unknown.
- **Fresh food prevents scurvy (citrus, vitamin C)** [`scurvy_citrus`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scurvy_citrus.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Rare, since voyages are short and people eat greens; it appears in sieges. The citron is an exotic, lemons and oranges absent. Cabbage and cress do the job. Elsewhere: Media and Persia, citron (Theophrastus' 'Median apple').
- **Deficiency diseases (beriberi, rickets, pellagra, goitre, night blindness)** [`vitamins_deficiency`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/vitamins_deficiency.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Greek physicians give liver for night blindness without knowing why. No idea of a missing substance: disease is excess, blockage or bad air. The poor live on dole wheat.
- **Variolation (inoculation with smallpox matter)** [`variolation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/variolation.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Smallpox is not clearly present in Italy; the first epidemic usually read as smallpox comes in AD 165. No material to inoculate with, no fear to motivate it.
- **Smallpox vaccination with cowpox** [`smallpox_vaccination`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/smallpox_vaccination.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. No smallpox to fear and no known cowpox to use.

- **Wound care (stop bleeding, clean, tie vessels, leave dirty wounds open)** [`wound_care`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wound_care.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Greek surgeons suture, splint, cauterise and dress with wine, vinegar, honey and resin; tying vessels is in Alexandrian books. Pus is expected. Legions rely on comrades and a few physicians. Local: Greek surgeons attending Caesar's officers; gladiator schools at Capua and Rome. Elsewhere: Alexandria, surgical tradition.
- **Antiseptics (strong spirit, chlorinated lime, carbolic acid, iodine)** [`antiseptics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/antiseptics.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Wine, vinegar, honey, pitch and verdigris go on wounds by tradition, not theory. Strong spirit needs distillation first. Surgeons do not clean hands or instruments.
- **Sterilising instruments and dressings by heat** [`heat_sterilisation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heat_sterilisation.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Bronze and iron instruments and linen can be boiled in any kitchen; cautery irons are heated anyway. Nobody sees a reason to.
- **Safe childbirth (clean hands, patience, cord care, forceps)** [`childbirth_care`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/childbirth_care.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Midwives (obstetrices), often Greek freedwomen, deliver on a birthing chair. Herophilus wrote on midwifery. Childbed fever is common; Cicero's daughter dies a month after giving birth in 45 BC. Local: obstetrices; Tullia, daughter of Cicero.
- **First aid and resuscitation** [`first_aid_resuscitation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/first_aid_resuscitation.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Not breathing means dead. Asclepiades was famous for noticing life in a man on his bier and proposed opening the windpipe in choking. Revival looks like magic.
- **Ether anaesthesia** [`ether_anaesthesia`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ether_anaesthesia.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Needs both strong spirit and oil of vitriol, and neither exists. Surgeons give mandrake wine or poppy juice and rely on speed and strong assistants.
- **Pain relief with opium and willow bark (laudanum, morphine, aspirin)** [`opium_analgesia`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/opium_analgesia.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Poppy juice, mandrake and henbane are standard Greek drugs, dosed by guess. Compound antidotes after Mithridates are in fashion. Willow bark is not used for fever or pain. Local: Greek drug sellers (pharmacopolae); Pompeius Lenaeus, translator of Mithridates' drug notes.

- **Human anatomy from dissection** [`anatomy_dissection`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/anatomy_dissection.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept low. Human dissection stopped in Alexandria two centuries ago; Herophilus' and Erasistratus' books circulate. Opening a corpse offends Roman religion, and Empiricist physicians call anatomy useless. Animals and wounds remain. Elsewhere: Alexandria, medical school and the books of Herophilus and Erasistratus.
- **Circulation of the blood** [`blood_circulation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/blood_circulation.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. After Erasistratus: veins carry blood, made in the liver, out to be consumed; arteries carry pneuma. The arm-ligature demonstration of vein valves costs nothing.
- **Physical diagnosis (percussion, stethoscope, thermometer, pulse count)** [`clinical_thermometer_stethoscope`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/clinical_thermometer_stethoscope.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Pulse lore after Herophilus, who timed it with a water clock; Hippocratic texts listen to the chest. A listening tube and percussion are easy. A thermometer needs blown glass tubes. Elsewhere: Alexandria, Herophilean physicians.
- **Tooth decay and dental care** [`dental_care`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/dental_care.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium.
